summary: Apple's framework is an out-of-process app extension that lets a developer inspect a crashed app (reason, binary images, symbolication, a read-only corpse port) and send its own report. BifrOSt captures crashes at the system level only: the shell's panic hook and the Linux coredump list. No app-facing SDK API inspects another crashed process or builds a report from it.

features.apple: CrashReporterExtension protocol, processCrashReport(process:), com.apple.crash-reporter.extension extension point
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 3 (theme-14, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No app extension mechanism lets an app's own code run when another app crashes. Apple's handler runs out of process; BifrOSt has no equivalent hook.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/crash_report.rs (CrashReason, ProcessCrash::reason); springboard/src/shell/diag.rs (CrashEntry signature, from crash.log); springboard/apps/console-desktop/src/model.rs (parse_coredump_list: SIG mapped to Fault)
features.note: The SDK's ProcessCrash carries the reason text and CrashReason displays it, tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-os-03.rs. Gap: the shell does not pass a crashed app's reason to an app's reporter, so the reason reaches an app only when the caller builds the record.

features.feature: Binary images and symbolication (binaryImages, symbolicateAddress(es), SymbolicatedFrame)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 3 (theme-14, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Symbolication is done by hand (coredumpctl and gdb, per the diagnose-crash skill). No SDK call maps addresses to symbols inside another process.
Mach ports are an Apple kernel mechanism. The Linux equivalent is the core file, which is not exposed to apps.

features.feature: Sending a report to the developer
features.apple: Extension sends its report to the developer's own server after collection
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/diag.rs (bundle shared with the developer, parse_log, upload_url, post); springboard/src/shell/diagnostics_page.rs (Diagnostics page)
features.note: The crash log parsing, the bundle layout and its HTTPS-only upload rule are tested headless in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01.rs. Gap: the bundle covers the shell only, and no app can send its own crash report through an SDK API.

features.feature: Crash record written by the shell and the runtime
features.apple: Framework-level crash data, collected by the system on crash
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/crashlog.rs (crash.log panics, last_exit, last_start, unclean-run note); springboard/mcp/src/dev.rs (panic_log)
features.note: Covers the shell's own panics and watchdog exits. Other apps' crashes come from systemd-coredump, not from this file.

features.apple: WebKit process-termination callback (closest counterpart in the Web content API, not in CrashReportExtension)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/webview.rs ("crashed" event, line 732); docs/bifrost-ui.md section "WebProcessPool crash recovery"
features.note: Web engine crashes reach the app as an event, and the browser restarts the engine. This is the closest SDK surface, but it covers web content only and does not produce a crash report.

features.feature: Crash log presentation in the Console app
features.apple: Not part of the framework (Console and Xcode Organizer read crash reports)
features.note: A system app reads the coredump list. No SDK API exposes it to third-party apps.

gaps: No app extension point for an app to run its own crash handler on another app's crash (the CrashReporterExtension role).
No SDK API to read a crashed process's reason, binary images or stack, or to symbolicate addresses in it.
No SDK API for an app to build and send a crash report to its own server; the only path is the manual diagnostics bundle.
Crash records for apps come from systemd-coredump; the SDK does not surface them to apps.
